conflicts.fact: Colour of cow's milk with universal indicator, and which cups are in the acid or neutral group
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 sorts the cups into reds/oranges (lemon, chai, Stoney), green (tap water) and blues/purples (baking soda, soap, Jik), and gives no colour for milk. Lesson 7 says milk turned yellow-green, with chai orange. Lesson 10 lists chai as red/orange/yellow with tap water as the only green.

conflicts.fact: Number of test liquids and indicators in Experiment 1, and the liquids tested
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 says seven liquids, replacing Stoney Tangawizi and Jik with vinegar (siki), against 'three commercial indicators' while listing four (red litmus, blue litmus, phenolphthalein, methyl orange). Lesson 2 uses the eight canteen cups against universal indicator, litmus, phenolphthalein and methyl orange.

Lesson 6 says Lessons 4 and 5 covered acid + metal and acid + metal oxide. In fact Lesson 4 is indicators and Lesson 5 covers acid + metal and neutralisation, and no lesson performs an acid + metal oxide experiment (Lesson 7 mentions copper oxide).

conflicts.fact: Whether lime used by farmers is calcium carbonate or calcium hydroxide, and liming reaction
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says Kericho farmers add calcium carbonate (limestone) to soil and that this releases CO2. Lessons 3, 9 and 10 say farmers use calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) as agricultural lime for neutralisation.

conflicts.fact: Why lemon juice differs from strong acids, and what Jik/soap contain (strong vs weak base), plus ammonia/soap
conflicts.versions: Lesson 9 says soap is a weak base and that Jik bleach is NaOH (a strong base); Lessons 1 and 10 treat Jik as a base without specifying; Lesson 8 and 10 give Jik as pH ~12-13 while Lesson 9 says weak soap gives pH nearer 7. In fact Jik bleach is sodium hypochlorite, not NaOH.

conflicts.fact: When the cumulative model was started
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says the running model has been built since Lesson 1; Lessons 4 and 10 say it began in Lesson 1; Lessons 6, 8 and 9 say it began in Lesson 3.

conflicts.fact: pH of lemon juice and ethanoic acid data source/values
conflicts.versions: Lesson 9 says ethanoic acid at the same concentration as HCl gave pH ~3 in Lesson 8 data, but Lesson 8 tested only the eight canteen liquids (not HCl, vinegar or ammonia). Lesson 9 gives ~1 in 100 molecules ionised for pH 3 yet lemon juice pH 2-3; Lesson 10 gives lemon juice pH ~2.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 8 count of reference liquids and Kericho item
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 overview lists reference values for stomach acid, lime juice, black tea, cow milk, blood, Lake Magadi and liquid soap, while its Observed section says six reference liquids including Kericho tea farm soil runoff, which is not in the overview list.
